chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Hammām, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a man upon whom a hadd punishment had become due, while he had many sores on his body. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Leave him until he recovers; do not reopen them against him and thereby kill him.”

key_terms.أَصَابَ حَدًّا: became liable to a prescribed legal punishment
key_terms.أَقِرُّوهُ: leave him and do not proceed against him for the time being
key_terms.فَتَقْتُلُوهُ: such that you would kill him
key_terms.قُرُوحٌ: sores or wounds on the body
key_terms.لَا تَنْكَئُوهَا: do not reopen or aggravate those wounds

ai.seo_question: Should a hadd punishment be delayed if the convicted person is physically injured or ill?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a man liable for a hadd punishment had numerous sores on his body, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ordered that the punishment be delayed until he recovered. It indicates care in the application of legal punishment so that it does not lead to wrongful killing through aggravating an existing condition.
